claims.text: The starting TiVNbTa is an as-cast, single-phase BCC alloy.
As-cast TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
As-cast TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K and 30% strain.
A solution treatment near 1800 K followed by warm forging or sintering will homogenize TiVNbTa.
The proposed processing will refine the BCC grain structure of TiVNbTa.
The proposed processing will increase the density of stable edge dislocations in TiVNbTa.
The thermal treatment will dissolve microsegregation in TiVNbTa.
A refined, uniform BCC matrix will favor edge-dislocation slip over screw-dislocation motion at high temperature.
Edge-dislocation-dominated yielding can support elevated-temperature strength retention.
The proposed treatment will raise TiVNbTa yield strength at 1273 K well above 330 MPa.
The proposed treatment will increase TiVNbTa compressive strength at 1273 K.
The proposed treatment will preserve or enhance TiVNbTa ductility.
The processed TiVNbTa will maintain adequate thermal conductivity for efficient heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
W and CuCrZr have mismatched operating-temperature ranges that motivate use of an intermediate layer.
The predicted improvements persist up to 1273 K and compressive strains up to 30%.
Operation under the stated 1273 K and 30% strain boundary will keep W and CuCrZr within their thermal and mechanical limits.

contradictions.description: The material-initial-state and baseline fields describe both 330 MPa and 423 MPa as yield strengths, whereas the prediction treats 330 MPa as the yield baseline and the surrounding formulation distinguishes 423 MPa as compressive strength.

The prediction permits ductility merely to be preserved, but the falsification rule requires improved ductility; unchanged ductility could therefore satisfy the prediction while triggering the stated falsification condition.
